subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance targets & benchmark methodology
messages:
From: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acmeai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmeai.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: performance targets & streaming requirements

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the call today — helpful discussion. Quick recap of our product needs and a couple of clarifying questions so we can scope the next steps.

High-level: we plan to use Redwood for a latency-sensitive customer-facing chat feature. Key targets:
- Concurrency: support up to 800 concurrent chat sessions for peak traffic (user-per-session model).
- Throughput: average of ~60 requests/sec sustained during peak; bursts up to ~200 rps for 30s windows.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile generation latency <= 200ms for short prompts (~60 tokens output) and <= 350ms for long streaming responses (up to 1024 tokens).
- Streaming: we need sub-100ms first-byte latency for streaming mode and steady token throughput of ~40 tokens/sec once streaming starts.

Questions for you / next steps:
1) Can you share a reproducible benchmark methodology and the exact prompt sets you’d run so we can validate results on our side?
2) Will Redwood provide a baseline config (model variant, quantization profile, GPU type) that matches the hosted performance you quoted?
3) Any special considerations for private deployment vs hosted (VPC) that would materially change latency/throughput numbers?

We can share a small sample of our real prompt distribution if that helps — I attached a short sample in the call notes (not shown here). Let me know when your engineering contacts are available to run an initial benchmark.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Taylor
Head of Product
Acme AI

Hi Sam — great to meet you on the call. +1 on the recap. I pulled together what we discussed and next steps so everyone is aligned.

Summary of asks (from Acme):
- Validate P95 latency targets: <=200ms (short) and <=350ms (long streaming).
- Validate concurrency/throughput targets at 800 concurrent sessions and bursts to 200 rps.
- Confirm streaming first-byte and token throughput behavior (sub-100ms first byte; ~40 tok/sec sustained).

What we’ll provide from Redwood:
- A reproducible benchmark harness and the prompt set we recommend as a starting point.
- A baseline runtime config (model, quantization, GPU instance type) that maps to our hosted profile.
- Run instructions so Acme can reproduce locally (private) or we can run a joint benchmark on Hosted.

Next steps / asks:
1) I’ll loop in our SRE/solutions engineer (Dev) who will share the benchmark harness and a short prompt pack we’ll run for the initial measurement.
2) Dev — can you include measurement definitions (p50/p95/p99, end-to-end vs generation-only), build/run reproducibility notes, and a sample results CSV we’ll use for side-by-side comparisons?
3) Sam — can you confirm the exact expected maximum prompt + response token size for the two cases (short vs long streaming)? That will help us pick model context and batch sizing.

We’d like to target an initial run by Friday PST if possible.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance targets & benchmark methodology (attachments)

Sam + Marissa,

Attaching what I promised on the call. Files included in the email thread below and also pushed to the GitHub link in the metadata:
- acme_prompt_set_v1.json (sample prompt distribution: short chat prompts and long-stream prompts)
- benchmark_harness_readme.md (how to run the harness, flags, common pitfalls)
- perf_results_template.csv (columns: run_id, model, quant_profile, gpu_type, concurrency, rps, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, first_byte_ms, avg_tok_per_sec, notes)

High-level benchmark methodology (summary):
1) Measurement definitions
   - End-to-end: measured from request enqueue (client send) to final token emitted. Includes transport and any gateway overhead.
   - Generation-only: time from model invocation to last token generation (excludes client/network latency). For Hosted runs we can surface both.
   - p50/p95/p99: standard percentile over all completed requests in the run. We recommend at least 10k samples for stable p95.
   - First-byte: time from request send to when the first response token is received. For streaming tests this is critical.

2) Reproducibility and harness details
   - Harness: open-source runner (Python) that supports structured warmup, steady-state load, and burst windows. The harness seeds the KV cache reuse patterns to match chat session locality.
   - Warmup: run 10 minutes at ~20% of target load to populate caches and JIT/compilation artifacts.
   - Sampling: collect per-request latencies and token rates, and output CSV in the template format.
   - Seed control: harness can accept a prompt-seed file (we provided acme_prompt_set_v1.json) so you can reproduce exact request streams.

3) Config mapping (what we’ll run as Redwood baseline)
   - Model variant: oak-2.1-medium (FP16) — this maps to the hosted profile we discussed.
   - Quantization: int8-llm-best (when applicable) — we’ll run both FP16 and INT8 to show tradeoffs.
   - Hardware: NVIDIA H100x2 equivalent (dedicated) for the Hosted baseline; we’ll note differences expected for A10/A30 hardware if you test private VPC.
   - Runtime flags: streaming_enabled=true; kv_cache=true; early_exit_threshold=0.95 (no-op control for now)

4) Test plan we propose to run together (we can run hosted or provide scripts for you to run in your VPC):
   - Short prompt test: 60-token output target, run at 800 concurrent sessions, steady 60 rps, 5-minute steady-state window, 3x burst (200 rps) for 30s. Collect p50/p95/p99 and first-byte.
   - Long streaming test: 1024 token outputs, run at 200 concurrent sessions, measure first-byte and sustained tokens/sec for 2-minute steady windows.

5) Reporting and artifacts
   - We’ll provide the raw CSV plus a visualization notebook. Attachments include perf_results_template.csv you can use to paste results.
   - If you want, we can run a 30-minute joint session where our SRE runs the harness against hosted instance while your eng team watches.

Notes and caveats:
- Hosted vs Private: network egress and VPC networking can add 10-40ms depending on region and egress path. For strict SLOs we recommend running an in-region private test to validate.
- Tokenization variance: if your prompt distribution has many short/long extremes, percentiles can shift — we recommend stratified reporting (short vs long).

Let me know availability for a joint run Friday morning PST (I can take 9:00–11:00). If that works, I’ll schedule a shared Zoom and a GitHub release with the harness pinned.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
SRE / Solutions Eng
Redwood Inference
